title: Seeking the end of a field sequence
statement: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $i<k$ index a work tape, and let $x$ be an input word. Let $ws$ be a nonempty finite list of nonempty words, and let $L$ be the sum, over the words in $ws$, of their lengths plus one. Consider a configuration $d$ in the running phase, and suppose that for every integer $p$ with $0\le p\le L$, tape $i$ at position $d_i+p$ contains the symbol at position $p$ of the concatenation of the words in $ws$, with a blank separator between consecutive words and no symbol outside that concatenation. After $L+1$ steps, the seeking machine is in the done phase with tape head $i$ at $d_i+L$; it is not in the done phase at any earlier time. At every time up to and including $L+1$, the head on tape $i$ lies between its initial position and $d_i+L$, inclusive, and every other work-tape head remains at its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ indexes one of the $k$ work tapes
The initial configuration is in the running phase
Tape $i$ agrees with the concatenation-with-separators tape at all positions $p$ from $0$ through $L$
